messages.subject: MSStats TMT, peptide-level output
parts:
Hello

I have just tested the latest version of MSStats TMT (from https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsTMT) and it is fantastic! Thank you! I have one question: is it possible to have, as optional output, the peptides rather than the proteins of various batches and TMT channels? Some experiments are peptide-centric rather than protein centric, so this would be great.

Thanks again

Oliver

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSStats TMT, peptide-level output
parts:
Hi Oliver, 

Thank you for trying MSstatsTMT from Github. Based on current MSstatsTMT, it is possible to perform peptide significant analysis. A simple solution is to use peptide sequence as protein name. See the following example code: 

library(MSstatsTMT)
head(raw.pd)
head(annotation.pd)
input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw.pd, annotation.pd)
head(input.pd)

input.pd$ProteinName <- input.pd$PeptideSequence

quant.pd.peptide.msstats <- proteinSummarization(input.pd,
                                         method="msstats",
                                         global_norm=TRUE,
                                         reference_norm=TRUE)
head(quant.pd.peptide.msstats)


test.peptide.pairwise <- groupComparisonTMT(quant.pd.peptide.msstats, moderated = TRUE)

Best,
Ting
